start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:hold-places-in-a-finite-pool with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and step hold on ledger ledger:p for subject person:sample-a with key sample-hold-a."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the ledgers, holds and waitlist are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.

2. Say "Run workflow:hold-places-in-a-finite-pool" with store, the step (open, hold, join_waitlist, release, expire, read or sort), the ledger, the subject and the idempotency key. Ask the person before you hold a place for someone they have not named.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts; every attempt must come out as the prove step says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run changes the ledger in one transaction through those objects and reads it back.

worked_examples.title: A place held, then the same key again
worked_examples.ask: Hold a place for person:sample-a on the sample class, with key sample-hold-a.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: ledger:p has total 2 and no holds yet.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "held", kept true, sequence 1; the same key again answers outcome "held" with the same hold id "ledger:p:hold:1", kept false, sequence 1.

worked_examples.title: A full class goes to the waitlist
worked_examples.ask: Hold a place for person:sample-c when every place is taken.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: ledger:p has two confirmed general holds.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "waitlisted", kept true, id "ledger:p:waitlist:2" at rank 1, sequence 2.

worked_examples.title: A release promotes the next waiting entry

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: person:sample-c waits at rank 1 on ledger:p.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "released", the waiting entry promoted: "promoted" "person:sample-c" into a confirmed hold, sequence 4.
